# Which Categories to Trust: Stability and Winning Margins

<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** Points, rebounds and assists are the most stable categories, so most of our 200 USD should go to them early in the auction. Steals, FT% and FG% swing the most, and threes and steals can be found on waivers, so do not pay extra for them. A category is only safe with a big margin, so build two or three categories that go together instead of being slightly above average everywhere.

## Stable categories and swing categories

Points, rebounds and assists are the most stable categories. They repeat from season to season at about 0.89. They also vary less from game to game. That makes them the safest base for a head-to-head team. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=368), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2220), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=401), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=2229))

Steals and FG% are less stable. Steals repeat at 0.74 and FG% at 0.75. Steals are also low volume. Even elite steals players can fall to 0.7 or 0.8 per game in a season. Expect few of last season's top five steals players to be back in the top five. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1144), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=794), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1534), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1662))

The percentages swing the most. FT% changes the most from year to year. FG% changes the most from game to game and week to week. In low-volume weeks each miss moves the percentage more, so results swing even more. One expert calls efficiency the most variable category week to week and prefers steady volume over a small efficiency edge. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=2135), [08-11](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=714), [09-16](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=1744), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1472))

Shot profile is sticky. Three-point attempt rate repeats at 0.92, and other attempt types are also sticky. Busts and breakouts mostly come from injuries and random shooting seasons, not from changes in counting stats. So treat a player's past percentages as less certain than his volume. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=309), [08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=436), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=58))

## Where the experts disagree

Blocks and the steals versus FT% question split the notes. One data set puts blocks with the stable group, at 0.86 to 0.89 alongside points, rebounds, assists, threes and turnovers. Another expert says blocks are very variable from year to year. On the most volatile category, two notes say steals and FT% are the top two. One expert adds that over the last two seasons FT% changed more than steals, because both makes and attempts move. Another calls free throws the most variable category of all. In practice, treat blocks as medium risk, and treat both FT% and steals as categories you should not pay a premium for. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1085), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1785), [09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1346), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=160), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2265), [08-11](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=714))

## Why winning a category needs a big margin

Each week we play one opponent in nine small samples. A small edge (a z-score of about 0.7) wins a category only about 55% of the time. A large edge (about 2.5) wins about 85%. Build big buffers in the categories you target. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1154), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=58))

Defensive edges are small in weekly terms. Going from 0.7 to 1.0 steals per game adds about one steal per week, which is easy to flip. Putting too much of your team into high-variance categories leaves you open to strange losses. ([09-10](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1169), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=88))

Being strong in both FG% and FT% is very hard. Barely winning both is fragile. Money spent chasing both leaves you short elsewhere. Good efficiency on low volume does not move a team ratio much. Since FG% and FT% swing a lot, punting one of them works well in head-to-head. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1264), [09-10](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1120), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1472))

This matters most in playoff weeks 19, 20 and 21. A short week with fewer attempts can flip a percentage category you were barely winning. Count on your stable volume categories, not on a thin percentage edge. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=2135), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1104))

## Which categories move together

Points and assists come together. Target high scorers and you usually get assists too, and the reverse is also true. The guard build (points, threes, assists, steals, FT%) is common because its categories support each other. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=531), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=552))

The big man build is harder. Only rebounds, blocks and FG% move together. It does not bring steals or low turnovers with it, and blocks and turnovers are not correlated. Threes and FG% pull against each other, so adding threes to a big man build is hard. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=819), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=878), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1031))

Steals are the swing category. They do not tie strongly into either build. A low-volume build of threes, steals, blocks, FG% and FT% is very hard to pull off, because those categories do not drag each other along. Players who combine categories that do not usually go together, like rebounds and assists, carry extra value. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=839), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1466), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1382))

## What waivers can and cannot replace

Threes are easy to find on waivers. About two threes per game is now league average in fantasy, so a shooter who hits two threes is nothing special. That is why non-shooters do not hurt you much in threes. You can stream threes later. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1512), [10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1214), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1744), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=569), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=636))

Steals are one of the most common categories on the waiver wire. They also create oddities in standard 9-cat rankings. Do not let strong steals alone push a player's value up. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1557), [09-09](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2462), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=2076))

Assists are very hard to find on waivers. Points, assists and FT% are the scarcest categories later in drafts. Points and assists in real volume are very hard to find once the early picks are gone. With 144 players drafted, the waiver pool will not fix a weak points or assists team. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1073), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1822), [09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=799))

## How this shapes our auction bids

Spend your largest bids on reliable points, rebounds and assists producers. Their production repeats more reliably than value built on steals, blocks and percentages. A low scorer bought for other stats hurts points a lot, since the average fantasy scorer gives about 18 points. A big bid on a low-usage, low-scoring player nearly commits you to punting points. ([09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=456), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=415), [10-01](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=331))

If you miss on points and assists early, do not chase them at the end of the auction. The scarcity note says you can punt them instead. Pick a build where the categories pull together, and aim for big margins in those categories. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1822), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1104))

Do not pay extra for threes specialists or steals specialists. A guard who only shoots threes and does not rebound or assist is a bad profile unless he is elite. A pure scorer needs about 28% usage and about 40% from three to matter. A scorer who is weak in steals, blocks and rebounds has too many holes for a standard league. Save your FAB and your 6 weekly adds for streaming threes and steals. ([07-05](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=3864), [07-02](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1695), [06-29](https://youtu.be/bHA-JoW3reE?t=805), [10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1214), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1557))

Treat percentages with care. If you buy a poor free throw shooter, price him for bad free throws, so any improvement is a bonus. Avoid flat profiles. In a 12-team league, average means roughly the 75th player, and a player close to average in every category can end up around 100th. Check that each player you bid on has a standout skill in a stable category. ([08-11](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=714), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1376), [07-23](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=1038))

Remember that small changes move value a lot. One extra steal a week can be worth about 15 ranking spots, and one extra made basket per game about 10. Going from 28 to 33 points per game adds about 20% of scoring value. Decide on purpose when you are bidding for safety and when you are bidding for upside. ([09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=2076), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=322), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=2169), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=196))
